s1.syndrome_frame: Acute right-sided chest and abdominal pain with dyspnea and fever
salient_findings: Sharp, tearing, localized pain worsened by movement and deep inspiration
Patchy, macular hyperpigmented rash on both shins and dorsum of the feet
Decreased breath sounds and vocal fremitus at the right lower chest
key_facts: 10 days of right-sided chest and right upper abdominal pain and dyspnea
History of recurrent low-grade fevers
Newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus treated with metformin
Temperature 37.2°C on admission
Heart rate 110 bpm on admission
Respiratory rate 40 breaths/min on admission
White blood cell count 12.3 × 10^3/µL
Chest radiograph showed patchy infiltrates in the right lower zone and obliteration of the right costophrenic angle
Thoracentesis yielded pale yellow fluid with 1260 WBCs/µL (87% neutrophils)
Pleural biopsy showed empyema without granulomas
CT chest revealed multiple encysted pleural effusions in the right lung

shortlist.why_kept: Pleural biopsy showed empyema without granulomas and thoracentesis yielded pale yellow fluid with 1260 WBCs/µL (87% neutrophils)

shortlist.label: Pleural effusion
shortlist.why_kept: Chest radiograph showed patchy infiltrates in the right lower zone and obliteration of the right costophrenic angle, and CT chest revealed multiple encysted pleural effusions in the right lung

shortlist.label: Pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with right-sided chest and abdominal pain, dyspnea, and fever, and laboratory studies showed white blood cell count 12.3 × 10^3/µL

shortlist.label: Anaerobic bacterial infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was treated sequentially with piperacillin/tazobactam and then meropenem, with gradual resolution of fever and clinical improvement

shortlist.label: Streptococcal pneumonia with empyema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with a bacterial infection, and empyema is a known complication of streptococcal pneumonia
